title: moms_last_voicemail_tapes
display_title: My Stepdad Threw Out the Only Recordings of My Mom's Voice — On Purpose
beats: My mom died when I was 12, and I had eleven cassette tapes of her singing to me before bed — that's it, that's all I had.
I kept them in a shoebox for sixteen years, moved them across four apartments, never once pressed play too much because I was scared of wearing them out.
Last month my stepdad 'helped me declutter' while I was at work — cleaned out my closet as a surprise.
I came home to an empty shoebox and a trash bag already at the curb, pickup already come and gone.
I asked him where the tapes were. He said, 'Some old cassettes? I figured they were blank, Danny, you don't even own a player.'
I didn't own a player. I was going to buy one. That was the whole plan.
Sixteen years of saving her voice, gone in one Tuesday morning because it looked like clutter to someone who never heard a single second of it. Tell me I'm not crazy for not speaking to him since.
